$comment: The stack profile: everything the change process has to know about THIS template that
is not a script. The process (the engine, which arrives with the forge plugin) knows no
directory name, no tool name, no port and no test runner of its own -- it reads them
from here, and a template for another stack ships a different file with the same shape.
JSON configures, Python validates: sdd/stack.py is the schema and refuses a bad file
before anything reads it (`sdd-engine stack --check`).
Two things are easy to underestimate when porting, and both live in this file. The
signals are specific to a specification layout: `contract_touched` means the name occurs
in spec/design/api.md or contracts/openapi/, and those six are the engine's own. The
path signals below are this stack's: a Flutter template has no backend/frontend split
and does have lib/ and android/. And the diff gates encode directory names: which paths
are behaviour, which are a screen, which are observable from outside -- those are the
right answers for this stack and nobody else's, which is why they stand here as data.
An empty list is a statement, not an omission: `trees.screens: []` says this stack has
no screens, and the gate that watches screens then stays silent by construction.
A missing key is refused -- the absence has to be written down.
WHAT `schema_version: 1` PROMISES, AND WHAT THIS FILE DECLARES BEYOND IT. The number
names the engine's MANDATORY key set (stack.py, `_TOP_LEVEL` less `_OPTIONAL_TOP_LEVEL`)
and moves only when that set moves, inside a window the engine opens by widening
SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS. The optional keys are the stack's to use or leave, so two
profiles at the same number may differ -- and every difference from the Flutter
template's profile is stated here rather than left for a reader to find by diffing:
* storage_contract, migration_mechanism, readiness, binding_target -- the four
mechanism sentences at the foot of this file. Declared on BOTH templates: the
engine keeps them optional for a rollout reason only, until every template names
them, and this stack has a real answer to each. tests/fitness/
test_profile_mechanisms.py holds each to the files it names. They need forge >=
0.1.55 (claude-marketplace#115); an older engine refuses the whole profile with
`unknown key`, and the PreToolUse hook reads this file, so every Bash call dies.
* suites.<name>.no_db_args and suites.<name>.junit_flag -- THIS STACK'S. The backend
suite needs a Postgres and answers without one as a named gap, and two runners
fix their own junit path (the suites comment below says why). Flutter's suites
need no database and all take --junitxml, so the engine defaults are its answer.
* ui -- ABSENT ON PURPOSE on both templates. It is a switch, not a section: without
it the design stage asks a person for the mock-up instead of drafting one.
Measured 2026-09-23 on forge 0.1.117: `sdd-contract --against-pins` in the
marketplace, with this profile and Flutter's as the pins, reports 0 findings and 0
drift -- the contract fixture carries every key this file uses.
name: fastapi-react-postgres

$comment: The script contract: the entries the engine may call, by fixed name, with fixed
semantics (the plugin's docs/script-contract.md). The engine does not know what technology
stands behind a script -- it knows that `check` answers 'will this template's CI pass'
with exit 0/1/4, that `test <suite> --junitxml=PATH` writes a junit, that `setup`
provisions a fresh clone. `check`, `test` and `setup` are required; `start`/`stop`/
`status` when `runtime.app_port` is set; `db` when `trees.schema` is non-empty;
`generate` is optional. Everything else in scripts/ -- lint, build, contracts, infra,
audit, hygiene -- is a component of `check` and is called by the template's own skills.
One entry per test suite `scripts/test.sh` runs, and the engine's evidence at the
level of a single test: the RED proof, the flaky re-run and the baseline all read the
junit the suite writes to `junit`. `args` are the arguments after `test.sh`;
`no_db_args` is the form that answers on a machine with no database (a named gap, not
a pass); `needs` is what the suite wants of the machine -- `database` rather than
`docker` for the backend, because Docker is only one way to have a Postgres
(APP_TEST_DATABASE_URL naming one the machine already has is another).
`e2e`'s junit path is fixed inside scripts/test.sh deliberately: the report path lives
in the script, so the two cannot disagree about it. Read it; never override it --
`junit_flag: false` says the suite is not handed `--junitxml`. `frontend` likewise:
vitest.config.ts names the reporter and the path, and a flag on the command line
would replace the reporter array and drop its options.
`check` runs every suite on the way and leaves these junits behind; the boundary
and delivery profiles read them instead of running the suites a second time.
`isolate` is how the engine re-runs one failing case alone (pytest node ids); a suite
without it cannot be re-run in isolation and the gate says so instead of guessing.
FOUR SUITES, AND THE TWO PYTEST ONES ARE DISJOINT. `fitness` is tests/fitness/ -- the
detectors that read this repository's own source -- and `backend` is everything else
under tests/ (unit, integration, tooling). They used to be one: the fitness modules
ran inside `backend` with no junit of their own, so a red detector and a red
service test were one red suite, and a RED declaration naming a fitness case could
only be attributed to `backend` (#62). They are apart in BOTH directions, because
the engine reads a case id (`classname::name`) as belonging to ONE suite: a fitness
case in two junits is attributed to whichever report was read last. So test.sh
`backend` and `--no-db` pass `--ignore=tests/fitness`, the backend's `isolate`
targets name the three trees it keeps, and tests/fitness/test_gate_parity.py holds
the targets disjoint and covering every tests/<group>/. `fitness` needs nothing of
the machine -- no database, no Docker -- so it belongs to every profile, `unit-no-db`
included, and check.sh runs it as a gate of its own before the backend.
NO SUITE DECLARES `allowed_skips`, AND THAT IS AN ANSWER RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.
The key names which of a suite's cases legitimately do not run, and it buys one thing
while costing another: a suite that collected cases and executed none stops being a
wrong record, and in exchange ANY run in which that suite skipped anything is filed as
incomplete. Measured 2026-09-17 against forge 0.1.62 -- no suite here can spend it.
* `frontend` and `e2e` skip nothing. There is no `.skip` or `.todo` under
frontend/src and no `pytest.skip`, `mark.skip` or `skipif` under e2e/, so there
is nothing to declare and a declaration would only change how a blackout reads.
* `backend` skips on every run, and that is precisely why it must NOT declare. The
engine charges a declaring suite for the junit's `skipped` TOTAL rather than for
the kind of skip the declaration names, and a full run on a machine with Docker
and a database already skips 24 cases that have nothing to do with a missing
database: 23 in tests/unit/test_entry_text_rules.py, where only an `accepted`
case carries a length, and one in tests/unit/test_log_content_policy.py, where
alembic's fileConfig has replaced the root handlers by the time it runs.
Declaring would file every green run incomplete (exit 4) under a sentence that
is false about all 24 -- and close_stage refuses a delivery boundary on exactly
that list when the run carries no classified gaps, which a clean full run never
does. No delivery would close again, on any host, under any flag.
* `fitness` skips nothing on a run from a checkout (316 of 316 executed, measured
2026-09-23), and it must not declare either. Its sources DO carry skips, each for
a tree that is not a git checkout (no index to read modes or a census from) or
a migration with no upgrade() -- conditions a declaration would not name, so the
first run from a tarball would be filed incomplete for a reason it never said.
* The blackout the key exists to excuse cannot happen here. tests/unit/ and
tests/tooling/ mark everything below them `no_db`, so the backend's `--no-db`
always leaves the greater part of it executing, and `fitness` never needs a
database in the first place; and the profile
that runs without a database, `unit-no-db`, is DEGRADED, where the engine already
excuses every suite with no declaration at all.
What must change before this answer does: the engine has to tell a declared skip
from an unrelated one. Filed as claude-marketplace#140. Re-measure before declaring
-- tests/fitness/test_gate_parity.py holds the assertions that keep this answer true.
Where a requirement citation may live, and the form it must take there -- one form
per runner, because vitest has no markers and Gherkin has no decorators:
pytest_marker   @pytest.mark.req("CR-2608-a7f3/R-3")
tag             the Gherkin tag @req:CR-2608-a7f3/R-3
in_name         the id inside the test name -- [req:CR-2608-a7f3/R-6]
tests/unit/ and tests/integration/ rather than tests/**: spec/design/testing.md
§ The UI smoke is not a traceability surface says tests/fitness/ and tests/tooling/
prove tools and structure rather than product requirements, so they do not own
citations. The old glob permitted precisely what that sentence forbids.
What a running copy of this template occupies on the machine. `app_port` is the one
port the application and the e2e suite contend for; the e2e suite additionally
TRUNCATEs the target database between scenarios, so two runs do not merely queue --
they corrupt each other, and the corruption reads as an application defect.
`container_runtime: docker` says the clean room may reap its own compose litter and
ask `docker ps` who holds a port; `port_variable` is the variable docker-compose.yml
publishes the database on, which the clean room sets to a port this run owns.
`cold_timeouts_min`: Docker pulls and an npm install from an empty cache are slow, and
a timeout tuned to a warm machine turns a slow clean room into a red one.
Path patterns, one rule for the whole file: a pattern ending in `/` is a directory
prefix; a pattern with a glob character is fnmatch; anything else is a plain prefix,
so `docker-compose` covers every docker-compose*.yml exactly as the old startswith
tuples did. `product` and `tests` are git pathspecs (no trailing slash).
behaviour: a path whose change means behaviour changed. Deliberately not tests/: a
test added on its own is a fitness function or a repair, and demanding a change
directory for one would train everybody to reach for the exemption.
screens: fnmatch patterns rather than prefixes because the frontend is cut by bounded
context (spec/design/conventions.md § Frontend -- where a file goes), so a screen sits
at frontend/src/contexts/<name>/pages/ and no prefix names every context. A prefix
tuple kept working after that recut and matched NOTHING, which is the quietest way a
gate can be deleted: it goes on running and stops firing.
observable: the surfaces whose change is visible from outside the application -- a
screen, an HTTP route, a migration. A context's services/ and models/ are deliberately
not listed: a rule with no route and no screen has no black-box surface, and a gate
demanding e2e from a change e2e cannot see is a gate people route around with a label.
operational: what somebody has to be told about to keep a deployed copy running.
app/ is not here even though backend_touched is on the other side: most backend
changes change nothing about operating the system, and the variable a backend change
adds is caught from the other direction by tests/fitness/test_documentation_is_current.py.
`scripts/*.sh` and not `scripts/`, for that same reason one directory over. The glob is
the boundary this repository already draws: hygiene.sh checks scripts/*.sh, help.sh lists
scripts/*.sh, and hygiene.sh says what the line turns on -- whether a file is a task with
a --help a person asks for. The .py files beside them are the internals of those tasks,
and ci_summary.py is not even that: it is called by a WORKFLOW rather than by a script,
runs on no deployed copy, and is described by no page under docs/. Under the old prefix
every repair to it demanded a docs edit that had nothing to write, which is a gate firing
where its own sentence does not reach; 2026-09-16 spent an EXEMPTIONS.md row on exactly
that. What the diff gate gives up is the demand that a .py-only change be accompanied by
a docs edit; what those files expose to an operator -- a flag, a variable, a --help -- is
held from the tree side by test_documentation_is_current.py on every run, diff or no.
cold_required: surfaces only a fresh clone can judge. A repair whose diff touches none
of these is fully judged by the boundary gate at stage close; the six defect classes
a cold run proves all live in dependency manifests, migrations, build configuration
or the scripts the cold run itself executes (the user's decision, 2026-08-25).
product/tests: the ratio of one to the other is the sharpest number the cost ledger
produces. golden-set/ is counted by half: the seed half is what a new environment
opens with -- a product decision -- while the fixture half is what the suites assert
about. Counting both as test churn made the ratio flatter than the truth.
archives: which of THIS stack's documents are dated records -- written once, never
edited after the fact, naming paths that were right on the day. `backtick-paths` reads
this and stays out; the engine exempts only the archives it writes itself, and
changelog/ was never one of them (no constant in paths.py, nothing written, nothing
read). Until 0.1.45 the engine carried `/changelog/20` as a hardcoded literal; the
declaration is this stack's now. `changelog/20` names the record and not the directory
holding it, so README.md and TEMPLATE.md beside the entries stay linted -- they
describe today and are edited when today changes. No entry here has a stale path yet;
the first directory move changes that, and the answer then is not an edit to a record.
Extensions whose contents a person reads as sentences, and whose backticked paths the
content gates resolve. The engine carries the stack-neutral ones (.md .json .yaml .yml
.toml .feature .html .xml .sql); these are this stack's.
The path signals: measured from the paths a change reaches, not from the words a
specification uses -- there is no normative document for a Terraform module to drift
against. The six specification signals (contract_touched, schema_touched,
screen_touched, rule_touched, contexts_touched_gt_1, new_context) are the engine's and
are described in .specconf/process.json; these five are this stack's, and
.specconf/process.json may condition steps on them.
`infra_touched`, `tooling_touched` and `ci_touched` exist for the same reason
`rule_touched` does, one floor up. Measured by the 2026-09-01 audit: infra/ is 2 135
lines, scripts/ 4 158, the workflows 968 -- together more than the backend and the
frontend combined -- and not one of them was named by any signal. A network-rule change
in modules/network does not occur in api.md, data-model.md or ui/, so it fell through
all three rules and landed on `default: p0`: the same tier as fixing a typo.
Why p1 and not higher: those trees have no normative document that could diverge from
them, so p2 would buy convergence rounds with no second author to reconcile with. p1
buys what was really missing -- the requirements and the design step at which somebody
asks "where is this to live".
`Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` joined two signals that already existed rather
than buying a sixth (#30). Until 2026-09-17 they lit NOTHING: a change to the image
the application ships as scored the same as a typo, and no worker could write either
file. They are not one class and are not filed as one. The Dockerfile is the
deployable artifact -- the `image` job gates it and `deploy` ships it -- so it reads
as infrastructure; docker-compose.yml is the Postgres a developer's `start.sh` brings
up, which is tooling. A sixth signal would have needed its own row in `detection.rules`
and its own entry in three `conditional` lists to say what these two already say.

backend_touched.description: the change touches app/ or alembic/

infra_touched.description: the change touches infra/ or the deployable image

tooling_touched.description: the change touches scripts/, .claude/skills/ or the local compose file

$comment: The one place a path of this stack lights an ENGINE signal: a migration file is the
schema moving, even when spec/design/data-model.md did not. The repair tail's safety
net reads this -- triage's forecast can be too narrow, the paths do not lie.
Article XII for this stack: the tools that have a script of their own, and the script
that replaces them. The PreToolUse hook refuses a runner at a segment's command
position (so `grep pytest notes.md` is not a run of pytest), and the session audit
counts the same table after the fact. `match` is a regex fragment on the lowered
command; `remedy` is the sentence somebody sees at the moment they have already been
blocked, so it names the script to run instead.
This template's own skills: the members of the implement fan-out that know the
technology, and the operational wrappers over scripts/. The engine's catalogue merges
them with its own skills; a name declared in both places is refused -- a skill has one
owner. `writes` is enforced after every dispatch by comparing `git status --porcelain`
against it: a member that wrote outside its list aborts the wave rather than being
reviewed for it later. The write sets are disjoint -- a gift from the layout in
spec/design/architecture.md, not an accident -- and that is what lets the members of one
wave run in parallel without colliding on a file.
DISJOINT IS NOT THE SAME AS INDEPENDENT, and until 2026-09-23 this file said it was.
Disjoint lists prove two members will not collide on a file; they say nothing about one
member's output being another's input. Every Python and TypeScript import in the
repository was resolved against the `writes` below, following a module nobody owns to
what it imports in turn: eight (importer, owner) pairs cross an author boundary. Five
are the RED direction -- a test author importing the app/ or frontend/src/ its
implementer has not written yet, which is the failing test, or build-backend's scripts/
importing a locator or a harness a test author owns -- and were already ordered. The
other three sat INSIDE what used to be called the first wave, unordered.
Two of them hang on one file: tests/_golden_set.py, the corpus locator
build-tests-integration writes. tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py and
tests/unit/test_entry_text_rules.py import it, and so does
e2e/suite/steps/guestbook_steps.py, through e2e/suite/golden_set.py, which no member
writes. Dispatched beside its producer, a reader imports a module that may be
half-written and its suite fails to COLLECT: a red for the wrong reason,
indistinguishable in the junit from the red it was sent to produce. So build-tests-unit
and build-tests-e2e now run `after` build-tests-integration.
The third is the same pair the other way round, and the direction chosen is the one the
files decide. tests/tooling/test_e2e_harness.py and tests/integration/test_e2e_reset.py
import e2e/harness/ -- but they are tests OF the harness, the RED shape between two
authors: importing what the e2e author may be about to change is the point, exactly as
a unit test imports app/. The steps' import of the locator is the opposite, a reader of
finished infrastructure, and that one cannot run beside its writer.
tests/fitness/test_wave_dependencies.py recomputes every edge from the sources and
refuses this file when a crossing import is unordered or the locator's readers run
beside it -- and refuses an `after` that no import and no RED rule justifies, so nothing
is serialized for comfort.
THE RED RULE IS DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM THE WAVE COUNT. Every implementer
waits for every test author -- all four builders name all four. That was true by
accident while the fan-out was two waves, because the wave boundary and the role
boundary were the same line; with two test authors in the second wave they come apart,
and a builder naming only some authors would share a wave with the rest. The engine
enforces the rule over every subset of the signals a repair round can narrow to
(test_sdd_process_config.py), so the profile says it rather than hoping for it.
No `consumed`/`produced` keys, though audit ticket E4-05 asked for those names: the
engine answered it with the keys it already reads -- `requires` against another member's
`produces` for a change-record artefact, `after` for everything else -- and declined a
second spelling for one fact (compositions.py `ordering`). `produces` stays empty here,
because the engine joins it to the change directory and a source tree is not in one.
`tests: never` -- an implementer may not write a test, because an agent that edits the
assertion that caught it is the commonest failure mode of an autonomous implementer,
and the cheapest one to make mechanically impossible. `tests: only` is the mirror image
and exists for one skill: build-tests-frontend shares the prefix frontend/src/ with
build-frontend, because a vitest file lives beside the component it tests; a prefix
cannot separate them, so the rule is a file-shape test instead of a directory.
`model: opus` for every dispatched skill: a failed cheap attempt plus its error context
bought a second full dispatch (30 to 100 turns) against a rate difference of 2.5x;
the user read that number and chose to pay it (2026-08-22). `fable` is never a default
here -- the only path to it is a recorded question with the cost in its text.
EVERY SKILL NAMED HERE IS INSIDE THE DISCIPLINE MEASUREMENT, AND THE DECLARATION IS THE
TREE rather than a key in this file. The engine counts improvisation, the escape hatches
and a runner `runners` refuses, out of a transcript; until claude-marketplace#211 it read
the parent conversation's calls alone -- 30 of 286 in one measured session, with 3 622 of
5 201 requests executing inside dispatched subagents, which is to say inside skills like
the ones listed below. The number it reported was a lower bound. The engine half widened
the scope, and the half that is this repository's is the statement that these eleven are
in it.
It is not a key here because the engine cannot be given one: `stack.py` validates every
skill body against a closed list, and an `operational` skill may carry `kind` and nothing
else, so a `measured` key would refuse this profile at import. It belongs in the document
the model actually reads instead: each SKILL.md carries a `**Measured.**` paragraph naming
the window its calls are counted in and citing `process-failure.md`, the rule it is
charged against -- because whoever is charged has to have had somewhere to read it (66 of
69 charges in one audited session fell on a reader nothing had pointed at the rule). The
eight builders reach it through the worker contract every dispatch hands them; the three
`run-*` skills are loaded in the main conversation, get nothing from a dispatch, and so
cite it themselves. tests/fitness/test_skill_measurement.py refuses a skill that carries
neither.

build-tests-unit.task: Write the failing pytest tests for the pure rules -- tests/unit/ and tests/fitness/, no database -- each citing its requirement fully qualified. Run them and see them fail.

$comment: `golden-set/fixtures/` is the FIXTURE half only. The halves have different owners
for the same reason they have different directories: the fixture half is sized by
what a test must prove, the seed half by what a person must see. One author holding
both is what produced the conflation -- an entry added to make a preview look richer
weakened a paging test that counted them.
`tests/conftest.py` is a file shared by the whole backend suite and therefore
nobody's; it stopped a whole change once (a TestClient base_url that changed which
cookies come back). `tests/_golden_set.py` is the locator, and it has to be here or
the fixture half cannot be added to: tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py makes
registering a new corpus file mandatory.
build-tests-integration.task: Write the failing pytest tests that need a database, plus any fixture they need under golden-set/fixtures/ -- never golden-set/seed/, which is the backend author's. Each cites its requirement fully qualified. A rule held by an index is proved by a concurrent insert.

build-tests-frontend.task: Write the failing vitest tests -- the pure rules in lib/, the generated-contract adapters, the screen states worth asserting -- each carrying its requirement id in the test name.

$comment: `test_scenarios.py` is here because a step module with no import line in it DOES
NOT EXIST for the runner: pytest-bdd registers steps through imports, and
tests/fitness/test_e2e_scenarios.py checks that. It happened in CR-2608-8e96
(Q-ALLOWLIST). `e2e/ui/` is the black box's second room, the same author because
the e2e-scenario gate accepts evidence from either room. `e2e/suite/conftest.py`
is this suite's infrastructure rather than its content: measured on CR-2608-6fb2,
35 of 51 scenarios failed on a fixture the e2e author could not touch.
build-tests-e2e.task: Turn the scenario seeds into Gherkin feature files and bind their steps, in business language, each tagged with the requirement it proves. No application code exists yet and the tests must fail.

$comment: `scripts/` is here because the human interface to a backend feature is part of that
feature rather than a separate product (CR-2608-6fb2, Q-31: a script that creates
the first administrator account had no member who could write it). `golden-set/
seed/` for the same reason: what a new environment opens with is part of the
feature, and it travels with the seeder that posts it. The engine holds the first of
those by name -- test_sdd_skill_gate.py `_SHARED_PLUMBING` asserts `scripts/` is in
THIS member's allowlist -- so the path stays here and the gap it left was closed on
the condition instead: see `conditional` in .specconf/process.json, where this member
now answers `tooling_touched` as well.
`uv.lock` joined `pyproject.toml` on 2026-09-17 (#30). The lockfile is in
`trees.cold_required` and ci.yml runs `uv sync --locked`, so it is tracked and its
drift breaks CI -- and until this entry no member of any composition could write it,
which made "add a backend dependency" a change with one author missing. The manifest
and its lockfile are one edit; `build-frontend` already had the pattern right with
package.json and package-lock.json.
build-backend.task: Implement the backend -- models, services, schemas, routers -- until the failing tests pass, plus any seed data scenarios.md asked for under golden-set/seed/. The migration is build-migration's; never edit a test.

build-frontend.task: Implement the frontend -- pages, components, hooks, lib rules -- from the screen specification and the frozen contract, until the failing tests pass. Never edit a test.

build-migration.task: Write the Alembic revision from the ordered operations in spec/design/data-model.md, parented on the head you read with ./scripts/db.sh status, with the backfill before any constraint that would reject existing rows. Prove it runs from empty.

$comment: The author of everything that RUNS the application without being the application.
Added 2026-09-17 (#30, #35). Before it, `infra_touched` and `ci_touched` lit a
composition with nobody who could write their paths at all, and `tooling_touched`
one whose only author -- `build-backend` -- it never dispatched. Three signals that
change the tier and summon two design steps, ending in a refusal after the work was
done. The engine's test_sdd_process_config.py recorded all three by name against this
stack; closing them is what deletes the entries.
The write set is `trees.operational` minus `alembic/versions/` (build-migration's)
and minus `scripts/`, plus `.claude/skills/`. That tree already grouped these files:
the class existed and only its author was missing.
`scripts/` is deliberately NOT here, and that is the one place this entry bends to
something older than it. It is the other half of `tooling_touched` and it would sit
here naturally -- but the engine asserts by name that `scripts/` belongs to
`build-backend` (test_sdd_skill_gate.py `_SHARED_PLUMBING`, bought by CR-2608-6fb2),
and a write set held by two members would break the disjointness that makes the
builders' wave safe to run in parallel. So the `tooling_touched` gap was closed on the
CONDITION rather than the allowlist: `build-backend` now answers that signal too.
Two members therefore serve one signal, each owning a disjoint half of its paths.
`.github/` in a write set is a real power and it is deliberate: CI is the gate this
repository is mostly made of, and a change to it that no member may write is a change
made outside the process with the process watching. `tests: never` still holds, so
the member that may edit the workflow may not edit what the workflow proves.
build-platform.task: Implement the machinery around the application -- the Terraform under infra/, the CI workflows, the image, the compose file and this template's own skills -- in the shape spec/design/architecture.md chose, until the failing tests pass. scripts/ is build-backend's, not yours. Pin every action to a SHA and every image base to a digest; plan Terraform, never apply it; never edit a test.

$comment: Vendor plugins this template assumes -- the ones a Flutter template would name here
(dart-flutter from flutter/agent-plugins, with its skills and its Dart MCP server).
The engine checks each `install` against enabledPlugins in .claude/settings.json at
session start and says when one is missing; it installs nothing. This template
assumes none, and that is a stated absence.
The rule for the first one, written before it arrives: an entry pins a `version` -- one
concrete number, never a range, a branch or the name alone -- and lists beside it the
`skills` and the `mcp` servers THAT version ships. A name resolves to whichever tree the
client's cache holds, and the other template found two versions of one plugin side by
side, the older declaring no MCP server at all. The engine installs and refuses nothing
on the strength of the number; it banks what each dispatch was handed and reports a
divergence from the pin (claude-marketplace#209). tests/fitness/test_process_pin.py
holds the rule, vacuously until an entry exists.
MCP servers the workers may use, keyed by the name Claude Code shows in a tool name
(`mcp__<server>__<tool>`, or `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>` when a plugin
bundles it -- `match` is the prefix regex either way). `refused` is Article XII for
MCP tools: a tool that duplicates the evidence role of a contract script (running the
tests outside the junit the gate reads) names the script instead. Nothing is refused
by default; the template decides. The two servers below are the process's own, and
they arrive with the forge plugin rather than from this repository.

design-data.notes: Today's entities: app/contexts/*/models/ -- the truth about the schema is in the code, not reconstructed from prose. The revisions in force: alembic/versions/. design-testing.notes: The suites: backend (pytest -- tests/unit without a database, tests/integration with one, tests/tooling over scripts/), fitness (pytest -- tests/fitness, reading source, its own junit), frontend (vitest), e2e (pytest-bdd Gherkin under e2e/suite plus a Playwright smoke under e2e/ui). A pure calculation goes to tests/unit or vitest, never e2e; a rule held by an index gets a concurrent insert in tests/integration. Run a suite: ./scripts/test.sh unit | integration | fitness | frontend | e2e.

design-plan.notes: The implement members this template brings: build-tests-unit (pytest: tests/unit and tests/fitness), build-tests-integration (pytest with a database: tests/integration, fixtures under golden-set/fixtures/), build-tests-frontend (vitest), build-tests-e2e (feature files and step definitions), build-backend (models, services, routers, schemas, scripts/, pyproject.toml with uv.lock -- never alembic/), build-migration (the Alembic revision), build-frontend (pages, components, hooks, lib), build-platform (infra/, .github/, .claude/skills/, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml). build-debug.notes: You write under app/, alembic/versions/ and frontend/src/ (never a *.test.ts(x)) -- NOT infra/, .github/ or the image, which are build-platform's and outside trees.behaviour. The machine, checked: ./scripts/preflight.sh. Suites: ./scripts/test.sh backend | frontend | e2e; everything CI runs: ./scripts/check.sh --fast.

storage_contract: A constraint the store enforces, declared in the Alembic revision and in the model beside it: a unique constraint, or a partial unique index over the live rows when the rule holds only for some of them. Postgres is the one arbiter between two writers; a lookup in the service before the insert is a race, because two requests both read 'not there yet' and both write. The guestbook has no such rule today -- spec/design/data-model.md, section Indexes and uniqueness, says so and why -- and a natural key, where a feature grows one, is a separate column with its own constraint and never the primary key (D-03 in contracts/invariants/guestbook.md).
migration_mechanism: An ordered Alembic revision under alembic/versions/, with an upgrade and a downgrade that both work, written through ./scripts/db.sh revision and read before it is committed -- autogeneration is a first draft. Never create_all(). Every schema change declares one of three modes in spec/design/data-model.md, section Migrations, Compatibility mode: backward compatible (deploy in any order), expand-contract (two revisions with the code between them, the only safe route for a rename or a narrowed type) or breaking (a window and an order written down). A released revision is never edited; tests/fitness/test_migration_safety.py holds the rules a diff can see.
readiness: GET /api/health answering 200 -- with the /api prefix, never plain /health, which the SPA catch-all answers 200 from the HTML shell whether or not the API works. It is the one probe: APP_HEALTH_URL in scripts/_lib.sh, which ./scripts/start.sh polls before it calls the application up and ./scripts/status.sh --json reads back later. The route is app/platform/routers/health.py and its promise is contracts/openapi/health.yaml. It answers for the process, not for the database behind it.
binding_target: The endpoint and the field it returns in the HTTP contract, reached through one hook per resource over the generated frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts -- a component never calls client.GET itself. The From where column of a screen document's Data section names the pair, the method and path and the hook, and stops there; spec/design/ui/guestbook.md is the worked example. A field the contract does not carry is a change to contracts/openapi/ and spec/design/api.md first, then ./scripts/generate.sh.
